title: 291. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Inverse Function Graph Reflection
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Reflection of a Point Across the Line \(y=x\)
questions.learningObjective: Determine the image of a point on the graph of \(f\) under reflection across \(y=x\).
questions.question: If the point \((2,5)\) lies on the graph of a one-to-one function \(f\), which point must lie on the graph of \(f^{-1}\)?
questions.explanation: The graph of \(f^{-1}\) is the reflection of the graph of \(f\) across the line \(y=x\). Reflection across \(y=x\) swaps the coordinates of every point. Therefore, the point \((2,5)\) on \(f\) corresponds to the point \((5,2)\) on \(f^{-1}\).
questions.hint: Reflection across \(y=x\) exchanges the \(x\)- and \(y\)-coordinates of a point.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the line of reflection that maps the graph of \(f\) to the graph of \(f^{-1}\).
questions.question: The graph of \(f^{-1}\) is the reflection of the graph of \(f\) across which line?
questions.explanation: By definition, the inverse relation is obtained by interchanging \(x\) and \(y\). Geometrically, this interchange corresponds to reflecting the graph across the line \(y=x\). Therefore, the graph of \(f^{-1}\) is the reflection of the graph of \(f\) across \(y=x\).
questions.hint: The line \(y=x\) consists of all points whose \(x\)- and \(y\)-coordinates are equal.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the effect of reflection across \(y=x\) on the coordinates of a point.
questions.question: When a point \((a,b)\) on the graph of \(f\) is reflected across the line \(y=x\) to obtain a point on the graph of \(f^{-1}\), what happens to its coordinates?
questions.explanation: Reflection across the line \(y=x\) maps the point \((a,b)\) to the point \((b,a)\). Thus the \(x\)- and \(y\)-coordinates are interchanged. This is exactly the coordinate change that produces points on the inverse graph.
questions.hint: Think of folding the coordinate plane along the line \(y=x\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify the symmetry line of a function whose graph equals the graph of its inverse.
questions.question: If a function \(f\) is its own inverse, so that the graph of \(f^{-1}\) is the same as the graph of \(f\), then the graph of \(f\) is symmetric with respect to which line?
questions.explanation: The graph of \(f^{-1}\) is always the reflection of the graph of \(f\) across the line \(y=x\). If the two graphs are identical, then reflecting the graph of \(f\) across \(y=x\) leaves it unchanged. Therefore, the graph of \(f\) is symmetric with respect to \(y=x\).
questions.hint: The inverse graph is the mirror image across the line \(y=x\).

questions.concept: Points on the Line \(y=x\) Under Inverse Reflection
questions.learningObjective: Determine a point that lies on both \(f\) and \(f^{-1}\) from a given point on \(f\).
questions.question: The graph of a one-to-one function \(f\) contains the point \((4,4)\). Which point must also lie on the graph of \(f^{-1}\)?
questions.explanation: Reflection across \(y=x\) swaps coordinates. The point \((4,4)\) has equal coordinates, so its reflection is itself: \((4,4)\). Therefore, \((4,4)\) lies on the graph of \(f^{-1}\) as well as on the graph of \(f\).
questions.hint: Points on the line \(y=x\) do not move when reflected across \(y=x\).

questions.concept: Finding a Point on the Inverse Graph of a Linear Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine a point on \(f^{-1}\) from a point on \(f(x)=x+2\) using reflection.
questions.question: Let \(f(x)=x+2\). The graph of \(f\) contains \((0,2)\). Which point lies on the graph of \(f^{-1}\)?
questions.explanation: The graph of \(f^{-1}\) is the reflection of the graph of \(f\) across \(y=x\). Reflecting \((0,2)\) across \(y=x\) gives \((2,0)\). Also, \(f^{-1}(x)=x-2\), so \(f^{-1}(2)=0\), confirming that \((2,0)\) lies on the inverse graph.
questions.hint: Swap the coordinates of the given point on \(f\).

questions.concept: Symmetry About \(y=x\) and Coincidence of Inverse Graphs
questions.learningObjective: Determine the relation between \(f\) and \(f^{-1}\) when the graph of \(f\) is symmetric about \(y=x\).
questions.question: If the graph of a one-to-one function \(f\) is symmetric with respect to the line \(y=x\), then the graph of \(f^{-1}\) is:

options.label: A
options.text: the same as the graph of \(f\)

options.label: B
options.text: the reflection of the graph of \(f\) across the \(x\)-axis

questions.explanation: The graph of \(f^{-1}\) is obtained by reflecting the graph of \(f\) across the line \(y=x\). If the graph of \(f\) is already symmetric about \(y=x\), then this reflection leaves the graph unchanged. Therefore, the graph of \(f^{-1}\) coincides with the graph of \(f\).
questions.hint: Reflecting a graph that is already symmetric about \(y=x\) produces the same graph.

questions.concept: Reflecting a Point with a Negative Coordinate
questions.learningObjective: Determine the corresponding point on an inverse graph when the original point has a negative coordinate.
questions.question: The graph of a one-to-one function \(f\) passes through \((-1,4)\). Which point lies on the graph of \(f^{-1}\)?
questions.explanation: Reflection across \(y=x\) swaps the coordinates while keeping their signs attached to the numbers. The reflection of \((-1,4)\) is \((4,-1)\). Therefore, \((4,-1)\) lies on the graph of \(f^{-1}\).
questions.hint: Swap the two coordinates, but do not change the sign of either number.

questions.concept: Inverse Graph of a Cubic Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine a point on the graph of \(f^{-1}\) for \(f(x)=x^3\) using reflection.
questions.question: Let \(f(x)=x^3\). Since \(f(2)=8\), which point lies on the graph of \(f^{-1}\)?
questions.explanation: The point \((2,8)\) lies on the graph of \(f\). Reflecting this point across \(y=x\) gives \((8,2)\), so \((8,2)\) lies on the graph of \(f^{-1}\). Also, \(f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt[3]{x}\), and \(f^{-1}(8)=2\).
questions.hint: Use the given point on \(f\) and interchange its coordinates.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the image of a point under reflection across the line \(y=x\).
questions.question: The graph of a function \(f\) passes through \((0,-3)\). After reflecting the graph of \(f\) across the line \(y=x\), which point lies on the reflected graph?
questions.explanation: Reflection across the line \(y=x\) interchanges the \(x\)- and \(y\)-coordinates of every point. The reflection of \((0,-3)\) is \((-3,0)\). Therefore, \((-3,0)\) lies on the reflected graph, which is the graph of the inverse relation.
questions.hint: Apply the transformation \((x,y)\mapsto(y,x)\) to the given point.
